ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle B=35^\circ$, and $CD$ is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$, then what is the value of $ \angle ACE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB,\\
it follows that $BC=AC$,\\
hence $\angle A=\angle B=35^\circ$,\\
therefore, $\angle ACE=\angle A+\angle B=2\times 35^\circ=70^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle ACE = \boxed{70^\circ}$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as triangle ABC with B, C, and E collinear, where CE is the extension of CB beyond C, and D lies on AB with CD drawn perpendicular to AB. From the text use ∠B = 35° and that CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Since C lies on the perpendicular bisector of AB, apply the perpendicular-bisector theorem to get CA = CB. Thus triangle ABC is isosceles with base AB, so ∠A = ∠B = 35°. Because ∠ACE is the exterior angle at C formed by extending CB to E, use the exterior angle theorem: ∠ACE = ∠A + ∠B = 70°.

再推理：因为 CD 是 AB 的垂直平分线，而点 C 在这条垂直平分线上，所以根据垂直平分线性质，CA = CB。于是三角形 ABC 是以 AB 为底的等腰三角形，所以底角相等，即 ∠A = ∠B = 35°。又因为 CE 是 CB 在 C 点向右的延长线，所以 ∠ACE 是三角形 ABC 在 C 点的外角。根据外角定理，∠ACE = ∠A + ∠B = 35° + 35° = 70°。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as having B, C, E on a straight horizontal line, D on AB, and CD perpendicular to AB at D. From the text use ∠ABC = 35° and that CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB. Consider right triangle BCD: since BD lies along BA, ∠CBD = 35°, and since CD ⟂ AB, ∠BDC = 90°, so ∠BCD = 55°. Because CD is the perpendicular bisector of AB, A and B are mirror images across CD; with C on the mirror axis, rays CA and CB are symmetric about CD, so ∠DCA = ∠BCD = 55°. Therefore ∠BCA = 55° + 55° = 110°. Since CE is a straight extension of CB, ∠ACE = 180° - 110° = 70°.
